cases.title: Release planning
lines: We need to choose Tuesday or Thursday for the release. I propose Thursday.
Thursday is agreed. That is the release date; Tuesday is out.

decisions.meaning: The release was set for Thursday.

expected.forbidden: Tuesday chosen, or only a proposal to release Thursday.

cases.title: Pricing
lines: We should start discussion on pricing next week.
Yes, there is a lot to explore. We have not picked a price or a pricing model.

expected.forbidden: Starting a pricing discussion or selecting pricing presented as a closed decision.
expected.other: Pricing remains open. No individual committed to an action.

cases.title: Vendor research
lines: I am Mira. I will compare the two vendors and send the costs on Monday.
Thanks. We will choose after reading that. Nothing is selected today.

expected.forbidden: Research assignment or a vendor choice in decisions.
expected.other: Mira comparing vendors and sending costs is an action, supported by sys_0000.

cases.title: Hosting
lines: Maybe we could move to North hosting. I lean that way.
I object until we know its backup policy. Which regions would hold our data?
Fair question. Leave the choice open.

expected.forbidden: North selected, rejected outright, or retaining the current host as a settled strategy.
expected.other: Backup policy and data regions are open questions; objection is not final rejection.

cases.title: Migration
lines: If the load test passes, perhaps we could migrate on Friday.
It has not run. Even if it passes we still need to decide. I will run it tomorrow.

expected.forbidden: Friday migration committed, even with a condition; the proposal was explicitly still undecided.
expected.other: Running the load test is an action supported by sys_0001.

cases.title: Renewal
lines: Shall we buy the premium support upgrade?
No. We have decided against buying that upgrade this year.
Agreed, reject the upgrade for this year.

decisions.meaning: The premium support upgrade was rejected for this year.

expected.forbidden: Buying the upgrade or an indefinitely permanent ban.
expected.other: Explicit rejection closes a question and is a positive decision case.

cases.title: Rollout
lines: We agree to launch on Monday.
A blocker has just come in. Cancel that Monday decision. Launch on Wednesday instead.
Agreed. Wednesday replaces Monday; Monday is no longer the plan.

decisions.meaning: Wednesday replaced Monday as the launch date.

expected.forbidden: Monday retained as a current decision. Historical reversal wording is acceptable only if explicitly superseded.
expected.other: One current outcome, possibly a separate explicitly historical cancellation.

cases.title: Rollout over two parts
lines: We have settled the release date: Monday. That is our final choice.
Cancel the earlier Monday release decision. A blocker means Wednesday replaces Monday; Monday is no longer agreed.
Confirmed. Wednesday is now the final release date.

decisions.meaning: Wednesday replaced Monday as the final release date.

expected.forbidden: The earlier Monday decision surviving as a current outcome.
expected.other: Neutral synthetic inventory padding forces a real production window boundary before the reversal.

cases.title: Decide the pricing strategy
lines: Let's decide the pricing strategy at next month's workshop, after we have the interviews.
That sounds useful. Today is only about listing questions, not choosing a strategy.

expected.forbidden: A future decision workshop or any pricing strategy shown as a decision reached today.
expected.other: Pricing remains an open question; agreement to discuss is not closure.

cases.title: Decisions: choose annual billing
cases.notes:
DECISIONS
Annual billing?
To discuss: remove the free tier
cases.context: This was an exploratory billing conversation. My preference afterwards is annual billing.
lines: Annual billing is one possibility. Monthly might suit people better.
The heading in my notes is a template, not an outcome. We have chosen neither and have not agreed to remove the free tier.

expected.forbidden: Annual billing chosen or free tier removed, supported only by title, question-shaped note, or after-meeting context.
expected.other: Monthly versus annual and the free tier remain open. Context has no citable id.

cases.title: Gate for deployment
lines: We are deciding a policy now: deploy on Friday only if security signs off. Otherwise keep the current version.
Agreed to that exact conditional policy. Security has not signed off yet, so deployment itself is not authorised today.

decisions.meaning: A conditional policy was agreed: deploy Friday only after security sign-off; otherwise retain the current version.

expected.forbidden: Unconditional Friday deployment or a claim that security approval already exists.
expected.other: A closed conditional policy is distinct from a tentative conditional proposal; preserve the condition and fallback.

cases.title: Naming
cases.notes: Agreed: the public product name is Cedar, not Birch.
lines: I have written our final naming choice in the notes.
Yes, those notes accurately record what we just agreed.

decisions.meaning: Cedar was chosen as the public product name instead of Birch.

expected.forbidden: Birch selected or ignoring the only source naming Cedar.
expected.other: Citable typed notes can legitimately supply the decision.

cases.title: Warehouse choice
lines: Could we choose the west warehouse? It is only a proposal while the inspection is pending.
The inspection has now passed. We choose the west warehouse; the east warehouse is ruled out.
Agreed. West is the settled warehouse choice.

decisions.meaning: The west warehouse was chosen after the inspection passed.

expected.forbidden: West selected on the basis of the earlier proposal alone; east chosen.
expected.other: Earlier uncertainty should not erase a later explicit closure.

cases.title: Delivery partner
lines: We have selected Swift as the delivery partner. The choice is closed.
Swift has withdrawn its offer. Withdraw that earlier selection and reopen the whole question. There is no selected partner now.
Understood. I will research alternatives. We will choose a partner at a later meeting.

allowed_optional_decision.meaning: The earlier Swift selection was explicitly withdrawn; no partner remained selected.

expected.forbidden: Swift remains selected, another partner is invented, or the research assignment is treated as a partner selection.
expected.other: A cancellation-only decision is acceptable if explicitly framed as withdrawal. Partner choice is open; mic_0002 commits to research.
